(308). i also saw a buick enclave bearing texas buyer tag (3137f19) which resting by a large, pecan tree at [roadway]. savoc rocha explained that they were in junction to transport an impounded car (buick), and while positioning the truck ([identifier]) which was pulling trailer (728359k) in order to load the buick, heather rocha who was driving, exited the truck to look back, [roadway], and the vehicle moved forward, hitting heather rocha on her leg, causing her to fall. the truck rolled, and hit a mailbox at ([roadway].), [roadway], where it struck a fence at 308 hackberry. the vehicle being loaded (enclave) [roadway], and struck a pecan tree, belonging to kenneth smart ([roadway].). heather was loaded onto the ambulance by (ems) personnel, and i asked savoc rocha to provide information for the crash report. savoc provided all the information, except for his identification, which i would need to complete the crash report. i once again asked for his paperwork, to which he had none. i contacted border patrol, who spoke to savoc by cell phone, and advised to detain suspect. heather rocha became angry, and unbuckled herself from the ambulance cot, and exited the ambulance. i advised heather rocha, the roadway needed to be cleared, and that i was calling a wrecker. rocha advised me, she would load the vehicle, and move everything herself. sergeant buscha provided security at the crash site, while i transported savoc to the kimble county jail. when i returned, i advised rocha, the best course of action, [roadway] away in her truck and trailer, and allow the wrecker to load the enclave, to which she agreed. i called for a wrecker (roys), and then rocha advised me, she would load the enclave herself. i advised her, the wrecker was already en - route, and she would have to speak to them. rocha paid the wrecker fee, and loaded the enclave, by herself. rocha was there an hour and a half, and upon going, ran out of fuel. i donated (4) gallons of my lawnmower fuel so she could go. eor 5408.

records.deidentified_narrative: on august 27, 2023, at approximately 1226 hours, police responded to the parking lot of extended stay america at 1015 [roadway] south for a motor vehicle and pedestrian accident. i arrived on scene and contacted d1 while safd-ems assessed the pedestrian (u2). d1 reported that before he reversed out of a parking space, he checked the rear , and did not see anyone walking behind his vehicle. as d1 continued to reverse back, u1's back side collided with the pedestrian in the parking lot. d1 stated he immediately exited his vehicle and checked on the pedestrian. i next spoke to the witness, who stated he heard u1's tires screech as if they were braking suddenly. the witness looked up and saw the pedestrian lying on the ground behind u1. the witness stated he stood by with d1 and the pedestrian as he called 911 to report the accident. i then spoke to the pedestrian, who stated he was walking from his truck through the parking lot when he saw u1 reversing back. the pedestrian stated he stopped walking as u1 continued to reverse back quickly. at that time is when the pedestrian reported being struck by u1. safd ems (medic 31) advised that the pedestrian had non-life threatening injuries. per ems, the pedestrian had injury to his right side arm area, possibly a broken arm. medic 31 later transported [medical facility] for further assessment. based on the crash investigation, it appears as d1 was reversing u1 out of a parking space (private property) he collided into the pedestrian who was walking from the parking spaces towards the motel building. d1 provided a valid texas drivers license and current insurance information for u1. the pedestrian also provided his information. d1 reported that u1 had no damage from the collision. i also did not observe any damage on u1 from the collision. i contacted traffic investigations detail (tid) and spoke to det. s. mena #2027. i provided det. s. mena #2027 with the crash details and he advised that tid would not be making scene. d1 and the pedestrian were both provided with sapd [case id] and advised that a crash report would be completed to document the accident. nothing further to report. bwc/coban available.

records.deidentified_narrative: the deceased identified as sylvia crosby rivers, south carolina d/l: 7658806 in her possession along with being positively identified by tattoos located on her left and right arms [roadway] of ih-40 near mm 176. family indicated that the last contact with rivers was on ih-40 at an unknown gas station. rivers was last known to be traveling east on ih-40 towards her sisters residence in south carolina. her primary means of transportation was [roadway] ramp off of ih-40. family stated that the vehicle was having troubles and may have been abandoned by rivers and her 3 canines. time of the crash is shown as midnight as the time of the incidents is unknown. rivers was found laying face up on the improved [roadway]. one deceased dog was located next to her, and the other was located further east past [roadway]. there were two bags belonging to rivers that were inventoried and sent with her to robertson's funeral home in clarendon, texas. there were no other vehicles identified with the incident. the incident scene was surveyed with a drone to complete the scaled drawing portion of the major crash packet. the postmortem autopsy indicated that the cause of death was blunt force injuries of the torso and extremities by motor vehicle collision. the autopsy indicated that the manner of rivers death was an accident noting that the pedestrian was struck by motor vehicle. preliminary findings include multiple pelvic ring fractures, compound fracture of left shoulder, compound fractures of right fibula, and tibia with large laceration. the vehicle was sealed and released to edwards towing located at 15180 w. business ih-40,shamrock, texas, 79079. the brother-in-law was the first family member notified and contacted trooper varner by phone on scene. the driver examination questions were completed over the phone with a female identified as rivers sister elizabeth crosby at approximately 1:40 p. m. the family indicated that rivers last slept the night or two before the incident and was stopping at gas stations trying to get her and the car back to south carolina and had no physical conditions or mental complications keeping her from safely completing the trip. rivers was identified as being upset along the route but had left 13 to 14 days prior with john randy deer only indicating that she did not want to stay with her sister. on august 22, 2023 trooper varner completed an interview with the witness who first contacted wheeler county sheriffs office.
